edges.notes: Rocky Linux ships Linux kernel packages for supported architectures as part of the distribution.
Rocky Linux on standard ports uses glibc as the C library alongside the dynamic linker.
systemd is the default init and service manager on Rocky Linux releases per project documentation themes.
Rocky Linux services are expressed as systemd unit files and drop-ins on default systemd installs.
Rocky Linux userland binaries and shared libraries are ELF on typical Linux targets.
GCC toolchain packages participate in Rocky Linux development and RPM build flows.
GNU binutils participate in standard Rocky Linux RPM build and link flows.
g++-built packages link GNU libstdc++ above glibc on typical Rocky Linux GNU/Linux flows.
Clang/LLVM packages may be installed from Rocky Linux repositories where offered.
Official rockylinux OCI images are common glibc-based bases; Docker pulls and runs them like other Linux images.
CRI/containerd nodes run Rocky Linux-based workload images pulled as OCI artifacts.
Rocky Linux is a common node OS choice for on-prem Kubernetes clusters seeking RHEL-compatible glibc userlands.
Rocky Linux bases are packaged as OCI image rootfs layers conforming to OCI image layout conventions.
Substitutable Linux distribution defaults for containers and servers (glibc/systemd vs musl/OpenRC field patterns).
Substitutable community RHEL-compatible rebuild distributions in many server and cloud footprints.
Substitutable community RHEL-compatible rebuild distributions; CentOS Linux legacy EOL vs Rocky active maintenance.
